catalog_locator: Sec. 3.4 Prosody, pp. 41-42 (PDF pp. 13-14); saved file the copy we hold; text layer
catalog_quote: We have found no minimal pairs that contrast with respect to stress. Overall, most words appear to lack a syllable that is clearly and systematically more prominent than others, either in terms of vowel/rhyme duration, pitch cues or vowel quality. Furthermore, quite a few words vary considerably from one occurrence to another with respect to the relative prominence of syllables, and further work on the post-lexical prosody of Elkei is required to ascertain whether this variability can be accounted for as patterns of phrase-level prominence. There is no indication that tone is used contrastively either. Finally, the available data does not allow us to make any well-grounded statements about intonation in Elkei.

new_statements.rule_in_words: No lexical word stress is identified: no stress minimal pairs, and most words show no syllable that is consistently more prominent by duration, pitch or vowel quality; the prominence that does occur varies between tokens of the same word and may be phrase-level. Tone is not contrastive.
new_statements.exceptions: None as such; the authors note that 'quite a few words' vary in relative syllable prominence from token to token and that the data do not allow statements about intonation.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, from elicited citation forms (about 200 lexical items, mostly nouns, one speaker, acoustic measurements); phrase-level prominence explicitly left for future work.
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes Elkei (elke1240, ISO elk; Laycock's 'Olkoi') from one speaker (Elsi Seina) of Talibili village, Sandaun Province; Laycock's 1968 and Lean's data came from Yili village and the authors note any differences could be dialectal. No separate dialect glottocode exists.
